claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm responsible for one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he still in school, college, doing A-levels, or in approved training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is still in college doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 17 and in approved education (doing A-levels), that's a positive indicator for eligibility.

Now let me ask you some questions about your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex working at all? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually he does work. He has a part-time job at the local supermarket - he works full-time hours there alongside his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail. Let me clarify:

**When you say "full-time hours," approximately how many hours per week does Alex work at the supermarket? Is it 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's more than 24 hours a week - he works full-time hours there while doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information.

Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Although Alex is 17 and in approved education (doing his A-levels), which would normally allow Child Benefit to continue, the fact that he is working **24 hours or more per week** means that Child Benefit stops. 

According to UK Child Benefit rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week, even if they're still in approved education or training.

I understand this may be disappointing news, especially since Alex is balancing full-time work with his studies. If Alex's working hours were to reduce to less than 24 hours per week in the future while he continues his A-levels, you could potentially become eligible at that point and would need to contact HMRC about your changed circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

The claimant is responsible for Alex, lives in the UK, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, but the employment situation makes Alex ineligible for Child Benefit.
